title: What If Earth Got a Second Moon?

scenes.text: What if Earth got a second moon? Earth already has one sometimes, and it never stays.
Small asteroids called minimoons get captured by Earth's gravity, and simulations suggest one or two are near us at any time.
The average one stays about nine months. Asteroid 2020 CD3, up to 12 feet wide, lasted at least 2.5 years.
Orbits are only possible within about 1.5 million kilometers, and the Moon and Sun keep tugging at anything captured.
A big second moon would tug on our Moon too, which could either stabilize both or slowly destabilize them.
A moon sinking inside the Roche limit gets torn into a ring. Mars's Phobos may be next, in 30 to 50 million years.

description:
What if Earth got a second moon?
Tiny minimoons are captured for months at a time, but a big second moon would have to survive the pull of the Sun and our Moon.
What should we run through next?
